recipes.name: Easy Chili Relleno Casserole
ingredients_raw: 2 (7 ounce) cans whole green chiles, drained

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Split chiles open and spread half of the chiles into the bottom of the prepared baking dish. Layer with Cheddar cheese and top with remaining canned chiles. Whisk eggs, flour, and evaporated milk together in a bowl; pour mixture over chiles and cheese.

Bake in the preheated oven until set, about 30 minutes; remove casserole, and top with Monterey Jack cheese. Pour green enchilada sauce over the top; return to the oven and bake until cheese is melted, about 15 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Chili Relleno Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This easy chili relleno casserole recipe has a layer of green enchilada sauce and lots of shredded cheese for a meltingly good, easy dinner.

review.reviewBody: SO good! I actually made this with fresh chilis instead of canned and there was no problem. It was great!

I’ve made this now 5-6 times over the past 6 or 7 months. We really enjoy it! I made it as written the first time except for the pan size and subsequent times making it I changed it slightly: I use an 8x8 pan and split the chiles open and lay them flat. I add a little more flour, salt and pepper, 1/4 tsp onion powder, 1/2 tsp each of cumin and chili powder, and use cream and some milk instead of evaporated milk. The photo of the recipe shows red on top, and I tried 8 oz tomato sauce a couple times and it’s good! I use just 1 can (11 oz) green enchilada sauce—also good. And I’ve used an 8 oz spicy tomato sauce ( El Pato brand) which is also good. Really, this recipe can be tweaked and it’s delicious! My husband, son and I like it and scramble to get to the leftovers first the next day!

7/7 of my family members that tried this loved it. I did make a few changes to the recipe, so I can't say that I would have given it 5 stars as written. Instead of canned, I used 8 average-sized poblano peppers that were roasted, peeled, stems and seeds removed, and cut into wide strips. I also used about 1.5 lbs of pepper jack instead of the 2 lbs of cheddar, which I'm sure lent itself to a more authentic Mexican flavor, and probably made it seem less overwhelmingly cheesy. I also added an extra 2 TBSP of flour and about 1 tsp of baking powder to the batter to make it a little more fluffy and less custardy. If I had used canned sauce, which I didn't because I always make my own, I think 1 can would have been plenty! This was as close as you'll get to chili rellenos without actually making chili rellenos. I'll definitely be making it again!

This is tasty, no doubt. I made it tonight, with a couple less eggs, a couple TBS more flour and a teaspoon of baking powder, plus a tad bit of salt and another bit of cumin. If you have time, mix well the coating ingredients except the egg whites: whip them to stiff peaks before folding carefully into the other coating ingredients. (this is how the tradish coating is made) Bake until golden brown. Heat the enchilada or ranchera sauce separately in a saucepan while the casserole is in the oven. With each serving, drizzle about 1/8 cup of heated sauce over it, add cheese, cilantro and a TBS of sour cream. This way the batter comes out more like tradish Chili Rellenos. A very nice touch: drizzle a squeeze of lime juice over it as well, or else put it on your accompanying Mexican Red Rice. You can put beans in with your rice for protein, or else add cooked chicken to your rellenos. While the latter isn't traditional, it is very very good.

I used 3 fresh pasilla chiles. I scorched them (not burned) on the grill, put them in a bowl covered with saran wrap for 20 minutes , then peeled the skin off and took out the seeds. I chopped them and mixed them with the jack cheese and egg mixture. I found that on 400 you only need to cook the casserole for 20 minutes or 350 for 30 minutes. Added 1 small can of tomato sauce on top and sprinkled a handful of cheddar cheese and cooked it for 10 additional minutes at 375. I also cooked it in a slightly smaller pan. My husband who doesn't even care for chili relleno loved it!

This was so delicious. I made it for some friends and my husband - they loved it! I served it with the Mexican Rice II recipe.

Tips:

I found that I needed an additional can of whole green chiles.

I incorporated some of the tips in the reviews. I poached a chicken breast, shredded the chicken, and added it on top of the first layer of cheese. I sprinkled salt and pepper, cumin, and garlic powder over the chicken.

For the egg mixture, I added 3T of flour and 1t of baking soda to make if fluffy based on the suggestion of another reviewer.

I also found I only needed 1lb of cheese. I mixed pepperjack and a mexican cheese blend.

We cooked this recipe and loved it! We love Chili Rellenos and this was just delicious! We used 1 27 ou can of whole green chilies and 1 15 ou can of green chilie enchilada sauce at the end. Also 3 7 ou packages of shredded Mexican cheese. 4 eggs and cooked it for 375 for 30 minutes. Then poured the enchilada sauce over it and sprinkled the remaining 3.5 ou of cheese. Cooked it for another 18 minutes. We used a pan a little bigger than 8 x 8 but not 13 x 9. We will cook this again.

I made this twice with chopped green chilies. I spread 1 can green enchilada sauce and 2 cans chopped green chilies on the first layer. Continued the recipe as directed. Topped the casserole off with red enchilada sauce over cheese.

My husband and I really enjoy this recipe. I omit the enchilada sauce; but once it's done, I pour a little green taco sauce over mine. I chop up olives and green onions and put a layer of that over the cheese. I always make more than this recipe does so I make a bigger batch of the milk/egg/flour mixture. I put all my layers down before putting it into the oven, so it winds up being: chili's, cheese, mixture of olives and green onions, chili's, cheese, mixture of olives and green onions, then the milk/flour/eggs mixture. I set the timer for 40 minutes and then once the timer goes off, I check for doneness and cook longer if needed (since I make a larger batch.) Someday I may try adding roasted, red bell peppers to the olive, green onion mixture. I like to serve this with Refried Beans. Ole'
It is very good however I made two changes for myself with my rellenos x. I like ground beef and onions so I added a pound of ground beef and a half a cup of onions, chopped.

Made this using 1 lb. of sausage and 8 eggs. I used canned chillies but added some Chipotle peppers in Adobe sauce. I also added some cheese to the egg mixture as well as over the top. it was incredible and definitely something I can eat on the Adkins diet. Great for dinner with a salad and leftovers for breakfast.

Hubby and I love the flavors (followed the recipe) except I did add onion and garlic powder. The only problem was it came out runny. It didn't set up at all. I think next time I will add 4 eggs as was suggested in one of the comments along with 3 tabs of flour and 1 tsp of baking powder. Hoping this will work. Any other suggestions would be greatly appreciated.
If it doesn’t, have beans is not chili
i used 3 eggs just one 12 oz can evap milk 8x 8 pan and 3 cans chiles (just preference) enchilada sauce may need to bake a bit longer in smaller pan

Amazingly delicious even though I had my doubts that 2 cans of chilies was enough. Using half of them, as the recipe directs, is not nearly enough to layer the bottom of a 9"X13" baking dish. So I was a good boy and did what the directions said, dividing up the pepper for two layers, and HOLY SMOKE was this dish goood! Three of us ate it ALL and wanted more. I imagine I'll indulge my curiosity and double the canned pepper next time, and likely serve it with refried beans. But just as it is, the recipe is perfection in taste and appearance. So glad I found it.
I used fresh poblanos and it was delicious!
Pablano peppers people! Chili Relleno eggs are whipped until they are almost meringue without flour or milk to get the texture!
I didn't use sauce...came out perfect!
If I make it again, I would double the chiles, and cut the cheese in half
Absolutely delicious! I make it exactly as written and it is one of my favorites! Thank you for sharing
